chunks: From Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, he said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

The root of obedience to Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) is contentment with whatever Allah does to the servant, in what he likes and in what he dislikes; and Allah has not done anything to a servant except that it is good.
ai.seo_question: What is the root of obedience to God according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the foundation of divine obedience as complete contentment (rida) with Allah's decrees, whether the servant perceives them as pleasant or unpleasant. This state of acceptance is rooted in the certainty that whatever Allah ordains for His servant is inherently good.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 15. It has been narrated that Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) saying:
The root of obedience to Allah is to be content with whatever Allah does to a person regardless of what he likes or dislikes. And whatever Allah does for a servant is always good
